measureRecords.whatItDoes: Continues Corte Madera’s special tax for local paramedic and emergency medical services for four years. It starts at $94.50 per residential unit or per 1,000 square feet of nonresidential floor area, with annual adjustments of up to $7.75 and a maximum rate of $117.75.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the four-year replacement of the existing paramedic tax, with the stated rates, restricted spending and annual public reporting.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve the new four-year tax. The existing tax continues only until June 30, 2027, when it expires.

parts.label: Rates and estimated revenue
parts.what: Residential units and each 1,000 square feet of nonresidential floor area start at $94.50 a year. Annual adjustments are limited to $7.75, with a maximum rate of $117.75. The Town estimates about $786,000 a year; this is an estimate, not a guaranteed amount.

parts.label: Four-year replacement
parts.what: The new levy begins ten days after the Council declares the result, replaces the tax passed in 2022, and lasts four years. Without approval, the existing levy ends June 30, 2027.

parts.label: Restricted emergency-service spending
parts.what: Proceeds may be used only for local paramedic and emergency medical services. That restriction is legally enforceable. The measure concerns the Town’s tax; it does not impose a tax throughout the entire Ross Valley Paramedic Authority.

parts.label: Annual report and audit
parts.what: By August 1 each year, the Treasurer must report the previous year’s collections and spending, service status, and money carried between years. Town property owners may inspect it free of charge. The ballot also requires annual audits and public spending disclosure.

parts.label: Approval threshold
parts.what: At least two-thirds of votes cast on Measure Q must be yes for the new levy to pass.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Extends Fairfax’s paramedic services tax through June 30, 2031 and increases its rates. The Town Attorney lists yearly maximums of $107.50, $111, $114.50 and $118 per residential unit or per 1,000 square feet of nonresidential floor area for 2027–28 through 2030–31.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the four-year extension and new rate schedule, with money restricted to Ross Valley Paramedic Authority services and annual public reporting.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this extension and increase. The current tax expires June 30, 2027 unless voters extend it.

parts.label: Four-year rate schedule
parts.what: The official Town Attorney analysis lists maximum rates of $107.50 in 2027–28, $111 in 2028–29, $114.50 in 2029–30 and $118 in 2030–31. Each applies per residential unit or per 1,000 square feet of nonresidential floor area. The short ballot question describes adjustments of up to $4 a year; the analysis supplies these specific yearly limits.

parts.label: Change from the existing tax
parts.what: The existing levy is $103.50 per taxable residential unit or per 1,500 square feet of taxable nonresidential space. The new nonresidential calculation uses 1,000 square feet, so that calculation changes as well as the rate. The new levy is estimated to raise $432,000 a year.

parts.label: Restricted paramedic services
parts.what: The tax continues to fund only paramedic and pre-hospital emergency medical services through the Ross Valley Paramedic Authority. Revenue must be deposited into a special Town fund; Measure R does not change the permitted purposes.

parts.label: Reports, audits and collection
parts.what: The Treasurer must report annual collections and spending, funded-service status and money carried between years, with free inspection for Town property owners. The ballot requires annual audits and public spending disclosure. Collection follows the time, manner and requirements of other county-collected property taxes.

parts.label: Duration and approval
parts.what: The extension covers four years, ending June 30, 2031. At least two-thirds of votes cast on Measure R must be yes.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Continues Larkspur’s paramedic services tax for four more years through 2031. It starts at $107.50 per residential unit or per 1,000 square feet of nonresidential developed space in 2027–28, with a fourth-year maximum of $118.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the four-year extension and increased paramedic tax, including the new nonresidential calculation and the stated rate limits.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not extend the tax; it expires in June 2027.

parts.label: Rates and nonresidential change
parts.what: The current rate is $103.50 per residential unit or per 1,500 square feet of nonresidential developed space, including a 50-cent county administration fee. The 2027–28 rate becomes $107.50 per unit or per 1,000 square feet, still including that fee. The maximum fourth-year rate is $118.

parts.label: Annual adjustment wording
parts.what: The City Attorney analysis describes annual increases of $3.50. Its yes-vote description and the ballot question allow increases of up to $4, while retaining the $118 fourth-year maximum. The extension is estimated to generate $834,000 a year.

parts.label: Restricted emergency services
parts.what: Money is restricted to paramedic services through the Ross Valley Paramedic Authority, including emergency response, training, medical supplies and equipment, and replacement ambulance transport units. The ballot requires annual audits and public spending disclosure.

parts.label: Expiration and approval
parts.what: The levy terminates automatically after four years unless voters extend it again. At least two-thirds of votes cast on Measure S must be yes. Without this extension, the existing tax ends in June 2027.
